title.narrative: ISA Size of Wales Emergency response to health crisis in Yanomami Territory

description.narrative:
This rapid response project aims to improve the local capacity of the DSEI-Yanomami health teams in Auaris and Sururcucu to respond to the healthcare crisis in Yanomami Indigenous Territory in the northern Brazilian Amazon. It intends to contribute to improving malaria diagnosis by ‘thick smear’ analysis and increasing the pro-active search for potentially affected community members to reduce the incidence and transmission of the disease.
The project will buy two microscopes and additional laboratory supplies such as reagents and dyes and improve the infrastructure of the health centre in the Kalisi community in the region of Auaris, through the purchase of a 15 hp outboard motor (i.e. a small internal-combustion engine with propeller attached for mounting at the stern of the health team’s small boat). It is necessary for the project to purchase this equipment due to the emergency situation, in which ISA can allocate funds and procure these items far more rapidly than SESAI (the Indigenous Health Department), and respond directly to the most urgent needs based on direct contact with the local indigenous leaders in TIY, thus potentially saving many lives.
Despite the Brazilian government’s efforts to prioritise removing 20,000 illegal miners from TIY and provide emergency healthcare, the problem is still far from being resolved. The Auaris region is currently experiencing an uncontrolled malaria outbreak. The health hub in Auaris registered 1,100 malaria cases between 01/01/2023 to 23/03/2023, in a total population of over 3,000 people - i.e. more than a third of the population in Auaris has so far been infected with malaria in the first four months of this year. The local health teams urgently need support to control this epidemic via improved infrastructure to reach the most isolated communities, and adequate medical equipment.
